title: The Illusion of a Perfect Metric: Why Evaluating AI’s Words Is Harder Than It Looks

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review and meta-analysis highlighting how automated metrics (both traditional lexical metrics and modern LLM-as-a-judge evaluators) systematically favor or assign higher scores to longer text outputs.

Review of prior empirical studies indicating that semantic similarity metrics and LLM-based evaluators inherit and propagate harmful societal biases from their underlying pre-trained models or training data.
Analysis of existing literature showing that LLM-as-a-judge evaluators exhibit a self-preference bias, favoring text generated by themselves or models with similar architectures.
